key_insight: SurfPhase recovers sharp, deforming 3D liquid–vapor interfaces from a few camera views by using a surface-aware neural representation and rendering pipeline, enabling accurate interfacial dynamics reconstruction where prior neural methods fail.
problem_solved: Existing imaging and neural-rendering techniques cannot robustly reconstruct sharp, moving two-phase interfaces from sparse video viewpoints, limiting measurement of interfacial dynamics in experiments.
method: Represent the interface with surface-aware dynamic primitives (e.g., Gaussian surface elements) that capture sharp, deformable boundaries instead of diffuse volumetric fields.
Train a differentiable rendering pipeline that fits the primitives to sparse multi-view video frames, enforcing camera consistency and temporal coherence.
Incorporate physics-informed regularization and geometry constraints (two-phase interface priors) to stabilize reconstruction from limited views.
impact: SurfPhase provides a practical way to extract 3D interfacial geometry and motion from sparse experimental video, enabling data-driven analysis, validation of simulations, and improved learning of fluid dynamics where direct measurement is impractical.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: sparse multi-view video -> surface-aware primitives -> differentiable rendering -> 3D reconstructed interface
Before/after comparison: diffuse neural-rendering result vs SurfPhase sharp interface reconstruction
Time series: sequence of reconstructed 3D surfaces showing interface evolution (animated frames or stacked snapshots)
Quantitative chart: reconstruction error or metric vs number of views / ablation of key components
paper_title: SurfPhase: 3D Interfacial Dynamics in Two-Phase Flows from Sparse Videos
paper_authors: Yue Gao, Hong-Xing Yu, Sanghyeon Chang, Qianxi Fu, Bo Zhu
